name: Maine
scope: Spousal support under 19-A M.R.S. § 951-A (general, transitional, reimbursement, nominal and interim support). No amount formula.
formulaText: No amount formula; the court considers the factors in § 951-A(5).
durationText: 19-A M.R.S. § 951-A(2)(A)(1): rebuttable presumption that general support may not be awarded if married less than 10 years at filing, and may not exceed one-half the length of the marriage if married at least 10 but not more than 20 years. A finding that the presumed result is inequitable or unjust rebuts the presumption.
eligibilityText: General support helps a spouse with substantially less income potential so both can keep a reasonable standard of living; transitional support covers short-term needs or work-force reentry; reimbursement support answers exceptional circumstances (economic misconduct or abuse, contributions to the other's education or career); interim support covers the pendency of the case (§ 951-A(2)).

durationTable.rule: presumption: general support term <= 1/2 the marriage

facts.text: Economic abuse by a spouse is listed as an exceptional circumstance justifying reimbursement support (19-A M.R.S. § 951-A(2)(C), PL 2023, c. 646).
Awards issued on or after October 1, 2013 can be modified on a substantial change in circumstances (§ 951-A(4)).

sources.name: IRS Topic no. 452, Alimony and separate maintenance

testCases.what: no amount formula; 16-year marriage: general support presumed at most 96 months
no amount formula; 8-year marriage: presumption of no general support
